Metrotown is designated in Burnaby's Official Community Plan (OCP) as a Regional City Centre.
The Metrotown Downtown Plan was adopted by Council on July 24, 2017.

The plan boundary runs from Boundary Road west to Royal Oak Avenue east and Imperial Street south, with a northern edge on local streets including Bond and Dover Streets; Central Park is inside the western part.
Kingsway, Central Boulevard, Beresford Street and Willingdon Avenue are the plan's main streets.
The plan's general land-use map shows high-density mixed-use designations around Kingsway and Beresford Street and medium-density residential designations in the surrounding neighbourhoods.
Specific locations for non-market and market rental housing are not shown on the map because those uses are permitted on all residentially designated sites.

blocks.text: Metrotown Homes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Community plans in Burnaby are adopted by Council as a policy guideline for considering rezoning applications, and designations can be changed by Council.
Site-specific zoning sits in the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw and Comprehensive Development plans, not in the Downtown Plan map alone.
Proposed streets, lanes and linkages on the plan map are diagrammatic and may be adjusted for a specific proposal.

blocks.text: Metrotown Homes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Non-market and market rental homes can be on any residentially designated site, so rental buildings are not confined to one block.
New institutional uses are considered site by site on any mixed-use designated site, not pre-mapped.
Metrotown Station is at 4401 Beresford Street, between Patterson Station toward Waterfront and Royal Oak Station toward King George.

blocks.text: Metrotown Homes: development and new projects

items.t: Burnaby's 2026-2030 Financial Plan was approved with a 2.9 percent property tax increase and capital investment funded in part from reserves.
Burnaby's 2025 total residential rate was $2.97749 per $1,000 of assessed value, of which the City portion was $1.55649.

Burnaby's 2026 residential utility fees list a detached single-family water charge of $652.33, with multiple-family water at $374.54 and sewer use at $436.00, and a 5 percent discount if paid by the due date.
The City of Burnaby is a designated taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax (SVT).
Metrotown Station is an elevated Expo Line station on Central Boulevard, with Patterson Station to the west and Royal Oak Station to the east.
Kingsway is the east-west arterial through the plan area, linking to Vancouver at Boundary Road and to New Westminster to the southeast.
Willingdon Avenue is the main north-south arterial, connecting Metrotown to Highway 1 and Brentwood.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Metrotown?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 15 houses listed with 1 sold in the month and 345 condos and townhomes listed with 35 sold in the month in Metrotown. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Metrotown a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 7%, a buyers’ market; condos and townhomes had a sales ratio of 10%, a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or coach house to a house in Metrotown?
faq.a: BC's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow more homes on many urban lots, but each municipality sets the details and many lots are excluded. Check the lot's zoning with the municipality before you plan a suite or coach house.

faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in Metrotown?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.
